notes:
Customer: mid-stage developer platform (internal devtools). Primary ask: an IDE copilot that is repository-aware and deterministic across versions. Wants low-latency streaming in-editor (IDE plugin) for completions and jump-to-definition; target: <50ms token turn for hot-path completions.

Key technical requirements / highlights: repo-level chunking + smart function-level context extraction; incremental embedding pipeline integrated into CI (embed on commit/delta); allow model/version pinning per-team (we must guarantee identical outputs for pinned model across deploys). Prefers on-prem or VPC-hosted vector DB - 'data must never leave our VPC' (quote from SecOps).

POC specifics: 2-week POC with a 40GB monorepo (JS/TS + Python). Trial plan: host vector DB in their AWS VPC, Redwood runtime in dedicated tenancy or private deployment; test two retrieval strategies (file-chunking vs token-window vs function-aware). Success metrics: top-5 retrieval recall >= 80% for dev queries; end-to-end suggestion latency under 120ms with hot-cache and sub-50ms token streaming for short completions. Budget sensitivity flagged — pricing deck shared.

Integration notes: GitHub Enterprise connector preferred (app), CI hooks for embedding, preference for incremental embeddings rather than full reindexing. Wants KV cache reuse across sessions and stable model pinning so code-style suggestions are reproducible. Interested in Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization profile that preserve completion quality.

Security/legal: SOC2 required, KMS integration for keys, audit logs and retention controls mandatory. Legal to review GitHub app scopes (deploy keys vs full repo). Request for a residency attestation and architecture diagram before infra sign-off.

Quotes / call snippets: "If the suggestions can be reproduced and we can pin model versions, we can roll this out to 200+ devs faster." "We cannot have user code leave the VPC for embedding generation."

Stated blockers: need architecture diagram showing where vector DB lives, SLA commitment for streaming latency, and legal OK on GitHub app scopes.
